original_title: NHL 27 Is Using AI-Generated Voiceover for In-Game Commentators, John Buccigross Says
summary_en: Veteran commentator John Buccigross has confirmed that EA Sports is leveraging generative AI for in-game commentary in the upcoming NHL 27. While the tech promises efficiency, it also raises questions about authenticity in sports gaming.
ai_analysis: The integration of generative AI into sports titles like NHL 27 signals a significant shift in how virtual broadcast booths are populated, potentially impacting player immersion and developer workflows.

en.title: NHL 27 Ditches Human Touch for AI Voices, John Buccigross Reveals
en.summary: Veteran commentator John Buccigross has confirmed that EA Sports is leveraging generative AI for in-game commentary in the upcoming NHL 27. While the tech promises efficiency, it also raises questions about authenticity in sports gaming.
en.body:
The roar of the crowd, the crack of the stick, and the familiar voices guiding us through every goal and save – these are the elements that have long defined the immersive experience of EA Sports' NHL franchise. However, a recent revelation from veteran play-by-play commentator **John Buccigross** suggests a significant technological shift is underway. According to Buccigross, **NHL 27** will feature AI-generated voiceovers for its in-game commentators, a move that embraces generative AI in a way that's becoming increasingly common across the gaming industry.

Buccigross, who is set to join **Darren Pang** as the new broadcast team for **NHL 27**, shared his thoughts on the Chirping Zebras podcast. He explained that while he and Pang are providing new recordings, EA Sports is also employing generative AI to supplement the commentary. "They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," Buccigross stated. "It's like 'Wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it." He also recounted a humorous anecdote where the AI, in its early stages, misidentified the hockey term "seats" as "chairs" in a crowd reaction line, highlighting the need for careful oversight even with advanced AI. "Words matter," he emphasized, noting that while AI can be trained to correct such errors, manual input is sometimes required to ensure accuracy and maintain the authentic vernacular of the sport.

## The Evolving Broadcast Booth

This move by EA Sports follows a broader trend within the industry. Generative AI has been a hot topic, often met with both excitement for its potential and apprehension regarding its implications. Titles like **Call of Duty** have faced fan backlash for using AI in areas like cosmetic item generation. Meanwhile, EA Sports itself has begun flagging the use of generative AI in the development of other major titles, including **College Football**, **Madden**, and **FC**, with disclaimers appearing on their Steam pages. While **NHL 27** is not available on Steam, the underlying technology is clearly being integrated across EA's sports portfolio, signaling a significant investment in AI-driven development.

## What This Means for Players

For dedicated hockey fans and gamers alike, the introduction of AI commentary in **NHL 27** raises several questions. While Buccigross himself seems optimistic about the efficiency gains and the quality of the AI's output, the community's reaction will likely be varied. Will this lead to more dynamic and responsive commentary, or will it introduce a subtle artificiality that detracts from the realism? The anecdote about "chairs" versus "seats" serves as a microcosm of the challenge: ensuring that AI-generated content not only sounds human but *feels* authentic to the sport it represents. The fact that **John Buccigross** and **Darren Pang** are the voices being used suggests a commitment to retaining established broadcast talent, but the extent to which AI will shape their on-ice narratives remains to be seen. The game is slated for a 2026 release.

## Looking Ahead

As **NHL 27** approaches its release in 2026, players will be eager to hear how the blend of human commentary and AI integration performs. The accuracy and natural flow of the AI-powered lines will be crucial in determining whether this technological leap enhances or hinders the overall player experience. Developers will undoubtedly be monitoring player feedback closely as they continue to refine the use of generative AI in future iterations of the beloved hockey simulation.

content_raw: EA Sports is using generative AI to create voiceover for its in-game commentators in NHL 27 , according to veteran sports commentator John Buccigross. When speaking on the Chirping Zebras podcast (initially spotted by Insider Gaming's Mike Straw ), Buccigross was talking about his experience working with EA Sports on the NHL games. He revealed that he will be in NHL 27, but EA also used generative AI to add voice lines as well. "They're using some AI now; they played me some stuff back of my voice," said Buccigross. "It's like 'Wow, that's pretty good!' If that means less work but the same check, I'll take it. Sometimes AI will get something wrong. One of the guys was playing it back, and a lot of these guys maybe aren't hardcore sports fans; they're video game extrordinares. They're not always up on the vernacular. So they're playing back my AI voice, and they're like, 'Score! And the crowd gets out of their chairs!' I was like, 'No, they're not chairs. They look like chairs, but we call them seats.' "So, little things like that, you gotta go back and listen because words matter. [...] But then you can make AI smarter; in the future they'll say seats, they won't say chairs. You have to manually put that in. That was kind of a funny anecdote from the process." Generative AI is becoming increasingly common in the gaming industry, despite some fans pushing back on it. Call of Duty faced backlash for using AI to generate cosmetic items such as calling cards last year, and now, EA Sports seems to be embracing it in many of its games this year. This year's installments of College Football, Madden, and FC all have labels on their respective Steam pages that notify players of the use of generative AI in development. NHL is not on Steam, so there's no such disclaimer. IGN has reached out to EA for comment on how AI is being used in the case of NHL 27 and if it extends beyond the game's voiceover content. NHL 27 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S September 11, 2026. IGN reviewed the game and gave it a 6/10 , noting that, although it's fun, it doesn't do much to improve upon its predecessor. "Hockey is one of the greatest sports in the world, and NHL 27 remains enjoyable largely due to that simple fact," reads an excerpt from the review. "The satisfaction of delivering a bone-crushing hit or snapping a wrist shot past a goaltender is just as effective as ever, and tiny tweaks to stuff like stadiums and music continue to add authenticity in small doses – but there are no illusions that anything truly substantial has changed this year."
